title: Deployment Pulse: cadence and release journal (Mar 2026, WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures the pulse-driven, incremental deployment cadence we want to standardize across smaller feature launches and mid-sized infra changes. It is intentionally lightweight: a short preflight checklist, a 7-day rollout calendar with daily observability gates, and a portable release-notes draft suitable for customer-facing comms.

Context / motivation:
- We observed long weekends with slow rollbacks when several small changes were released without uniform cadence.
- Goal: reduce cognitive load during launches by standardizing daily signal checks, clear abort criteria, and a short ops journal for quick handoffs.
- Applies to: mid-tier releases (non-major, non-breaking schema changes) and infra ramp adjustments that touch serving/runtime or routing.

Quick definitions:
- Pulse window: 24h monitoring window after a step where we collect traffic, latency, error-rate, and quality signals.
- Light canary: 0.5–2% traffic with KV cache warming allowed.
- Pulse gate: pre-defined metric thresholds that must hold for 3 consecutive hours before proceeding.

Preflight checklist (obligatory, keep binary pass/fail):
- [ ] Release branch built and integration tests green (PR link + SHA)
- [ ] Smoke test suite (deck-smoke) run on staging and results attached
- [ ] Observability dashboards copied to release dashboard (latency, p50/90/99, token-per-request, error-rate, model-fallbacks)
- [ ] Alert pages and on-call rotations confirmed for the 72h window
- [ ] Rollback artifact/version ready and validated (document SHA and rollback play)
- [ ] Canary config created (traffic percents, regions, model-variant map)
- [ ] Communication plan: slack channel, recurring 09:00 daily standup invite, stakeholders list
- [ ] Data retention & privacy check - no additional data exposure in this change

7-day pulse rollout calendar (example timeline - adjust per release size):
Day 0 - Launch prep (09:00):
- Final gating meeting (owners: release lead, SRE, Product PM, Feature owner)
- Start light canary (1% traffic, single region)
- Begin ops journal entry: baseline metrics snapshot attached
- Hold for first 4-hour pulse gate

Day 0 - Evening (21:00):
- Evaluate 12h signals (error spikes, p99 regression, token inflation)
- If gate failed -> immediate rollback; if marginal -> reduce to 0.5% and extend pulse

Day 1 - Expand (09:00):
- If all gates pass, expand to 5% and open second region (if multi-region release)
- Run downstream E2E smoke: routing, cache priming, KV lookups
- Check quality sampling (5 live prompts) and manual spot-checks on outputs

Day 2 - Monitor (every 6h):
- Keep at 5% for 48h while checking quality regressions, cost delta, and rate-limited errors
- If any quality alert triggers (see gating below) -> pause expansion and convene triage

Day 4 - Broadening (09:00):
- Expand to 25% if all pulse gates held. Turn on latency SLO tracking for production buckets
- Trigger canary-to-bulk checklist (cache warmers, batch adjustments)

Day 6 - Full ramp decision (09:00):
- Decision meeting with Release committee: proceed to 100% or hold/rollback
- If proceed, schedule slow ramp to 100% with continued 24h post-ramp monitoring

Abort and rollback criteria (binary conditions for immediate action):
- >3x baseline p99 latency sustained for 30 minutes
- Error-rate increase > 0.5 percentage points absolute or >200% relative from baseline in any primary region
- Token inflation > 35% leading to cost concerns without quality improvement
- Reproducible correctness regression found in production prompt set (see linked eval set id)
- Cascading downstream failures (queue saturation, rejected connections)

Observability signals (what to watch and where):
- Latency: p50/p90/p99, token-level latency, cold-vs-warm delta (dashboard: RELEASE-PULSE-LAT)
- Errors: 4xx/5xx splits, model-fallback events, degraded-inference flags (RELEASE-PULSE-ERR)
- Quality: prompt-eval pass rate on sample set, hallucination markers, regression alerts (EVAL-PULSE)
- Cost: tokens-per-request, GPU-hours delta (COST-PULSE)
- User impact indicators: dropped flows, increased retry counts, customer tickets tied to endpoints

Release notes draft (short customer-facing blurb, keep conservative):
Title: Incremental rollout: faster latency routing and stability improvements
Summary:
- What: Small, incremental update that improves routing heuristics and cache warm paths to reduce tail latency for the text/generate API.
- Why: Observed tail latency under specific routing mixes; this change reorders routing preference to prefer warmed-model replicas for short sequences.
- Impact: Expected p99 improvements for short sequences, no API contract changes. Customers should see improved responsiveness on small-batch generation.

Technical highlights (for release appendix):
- Introduced preference logic in SmartRouter to favor warmed-serving lanes for sequence <=128 tokens
- Adjusted KV cache priming to pre-warm on low-latency replicas using historical prefix signals
- Minor runtime patch to reduce memory copies in beam sampler path

Known issues and mitigations:
- Observed a transient spike in warmup traffic in region eu-west-1 during early canary (mitigation: throttle prewarm to 3x baseline and extend warmup window)
- Very rare prompt scoring drift on legacy model v1.4 - mitigation: routing fallback to v1.3 for flagged customer segments

Rollback playbook (compact):
- Trigger: Abort criteria met or unanimous decision at decision meeting
- Action steps:
  1) Switch routing rule to previous variant (config id: routing-v2026-11) via feature-flag flip (takes ~30s)
  2) Trigger blue/green revert for worker pool with prepared image (revert image tag: release-pre-2026-11-14)
  3) Inform on-call and set tickets: create rollout-rollback JIRA with auto-attach logs
  4) Run immediate post-rollback validation: smoke suite + 15 representative prompts

Ops journal template (for handoff and postmortem):
- release-id: short id, pr-sha, release lead
- start/end times
- pulse snapshots (baseline, day0-post, day2, day6) with key metrics as bullet list
- anomalies observed and mitigations applied (timestamp + actor)
- communications sent (slack thread link, customer email draft id)
- rollback? yes/no, timeline, root cause hypothesis

Day-of-ops – rapid checklist (one-pager for the release chat):
- 08:30: Quick triage: confirm all preflight checks green
- 09:00: Release lead posts start message in #release-pulse channel (template below)
- 09:05–09:10: SRE runs smoke walkthrough and posts acceptance
- Every 4 hours: update pulse channel with p99, error-rate, cost delta, and quality pass-rate
- 21:00: Evening check-in and decision to continue / throttle / rollback if needed

Communication templates (short):
- Slack start: "[release-id] Starting incremental deployment. Light canary 1% traffic in us-west. Release lead: Sofia Patel. Watch RELEASE-PULSE-LAT and RELEASE-PULSE-ERR dashboards. Escalation: @oncall-sre."
- Customer note (post-stable): "We rolled out an incremental update to routing and cache warm paths to improve latency for short sequences. No API changes. Please open a ticket if you observe regressions."

Open questions / follow-ups (for next revision):
- Should pulse gates use relative or absolute thresholds for p99? Proposal: absolute when baseline stable, relative for volatile endpoints.
- Automate daily pulse summary into a release doc (small Lambda to snapshot dashboards) — explore in Q2 tools backlog.
- Add a lightweight synthetic prompt harness to run during canary and report a single quality score every hour.

Appendix: short checklist of owners and contact points:
- Release lead: Sofia Patel (slack: @sofia.p)
- SRE on-call: Miguel Reyes (slack: @miguel.r; pager: +1-555-0124)
- Product/PM: Priya Nambiar (slack: @priya.n)
- Feature author: Lena Fischer (slack: @lena.f)

End of draft.

Notes: Keep this doc minimal and portable. For large launches follow the full launch runbook. This file intentionally focuses on a lightweight pulse cadence for mid-sized changes and should be referenced alongside the canonical release runbook linked in linked_artifacts.
